rgb: In the first two frames, the camera wearer stands at the threshold of open wooden double doors facing an outdoor paved area, with a portable table saw directly in front and below eye level at about 3.0 to 5.0 metres (out of arm's reach) as the wearer's left hand moves a narrow wooden strip from the right side of the saw table in frame 1 to the left side in frame 2, while the wearer's lower body is partly cut off at the bottom edge. In frame 3, the wearer turns roughly 180 degrees toward the indoor workspace, bringing the open wooden door and a floor-mounted yellow miter saw (about 1.5 to 2.0 metres away) to the left, a dusty concrete floor below, and an indoor area ahead containing a large wooden structure on the right and vertical boards leaning against a central pillar about 0.5 to 1.5 metres away. Across frames 3 to 5, the wearer steps backward into the room, moving away from a second person in a grey shirt and dark pants who stands beside the wooden structure, increasing the distance between them from about 1.5 to 2.0 metres in frame 3 to roughly 3.0 metres on the front-right in frame 5. This second person remains bent over facing the wooden structure to the right, looking downward at wooden panels out of their own arm's reach and toward the camera wearer. About 3.0 to 5.0 metres to the left of that person lie a black cable reel and scrap wood on the floor (about 1.5 to 2.0 metres ahead of the wearer in frame 5), while the vertical boards against the pillar sit about 2.5 metres ahead and a blue folding chair beside dark platform blocks is positioned 0.5 to 1.5 metres away to the front-left. As the wearer retreats and turns slightly rightward in frames 4 and 5, the wooden structure on the right becomes partially cropped by the right frame boundary, and the yellow miter saw on the left retreats out of view past the bottom-left edge.
depth: The depth map captures a transition from an open doorway looking outdoors in frames 1–2—where the camera wearer stands out of arm's reach (~3.0–5.0 m) above a table saw in front of them, flanked by open wooden door leaves to the right and left—to an indoor workshop in frames 3–5 as the wearer turns ~180 degrees and steps outward. In frames 1–2, the wearer's extended left arm and a thin wooden strip held in their hand appear brightest (~3.0–5.0 m), the table saw sits at ~3.0–5.0 m below and in front of the viewpoint, and the outdoor ground slopes away into dark foreground (~0.5–1.5 m). As the wearer turns into the room in frames 3–5, the left-side doorframe passes far away on the left (~3.0–5.0 m) while the interior layout emerges: a wooden bench structure and a crouched coworker on the right (~1.5–2.2 m away, moving farther to ~1.8–3.0 m by frame 5), a vertical stack of white boards in the upper-middle foreground (~0.5–1.5 m, ~1.5 m in front of the coworker), a yellow miter saw on the floor to the lower left (~1.5–2.0 m), and a blue chair closer to the left (~0.5–1.5 m, ~1.5 m left of the board stack). The coworker bends forward facing downward toward the wooden structure on the right, keeping the wooden panels out of their arm's reach while looking toward the camera wearer, and is partially occluded at the frame edges in frame 5. The depth map makes the continuous 3D floor gradient, the vertical relief of the leaning board stack, and the relative distance gap between the background door jamb and foreground objects much easier to judge than in the dark, high-contrast RGB frames, though it is unreliable on thin floor cables, fine wood scraps, and the dark indoor shadow of frame 3 where the coworker and bench blend into mid-grey.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a sparse subset of background and mid-ground entities—specifically `person` masks and a single `chair` mask—while omitting the doorway, table saw, wooden boards, miter saw, and floor layout entirely. In frames 1–3, a pink `person` mask at the bottom edge marks the camera wearer's own lower torso, feet, and extended left arm (~3.0–5.0 m below and in front of the camera, out of immediate arm's reach of the unsegmented table saw in frames 1–2 and partially cropped by the bottom frame boundary), documenting the wearer's arm extending forward in frame 2 and retracting as they turn indoors in frame 3. In frames 4–5, a `person` mask identifies the crouched coworker to the right of center at roughly 1.5–3.0 m distance, bending forward and facing downward toward the right (looking toward the camera wearer), as their relative position shifts downward and rightward into farther range (~3.0 m) as the wearer moves away. In frame 4 only, a purple `chair` mask detects the blue folding chair in the upper-left foreground (~0.5–1.5 m from the wearer, ~2.0 m to the left of the coworker and just left of the occluding board stack). While this map cleanly separates the wearer's self-body silhouette and the coworker's bent contour from cluttered workshop backgrounds that are visually busy in RGB, it is highly unreliable across the strip: it misses the coworker and foreground chair completely in frame 3, drops the camera wearer's visible left foot at the bottom of frames 4–5, loses the chair in frame 5, and fails to segment any tools, lumber, or structural surfaces.
pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single magenta left-hand skeleton for the camera wearer in the lower-right quadrant of frame 1. In frame 1, this hand skeleton lies ~3.0–5.0 m below and slightly right of center in front of the camera wearer, gripping the thin wooden strip out of arm's reach just above the table saw (~3.0–5.0 m away), with the fingers curled inward and oriented forward and slightly right. The map provides no spatial data on the scene layout, the doorway, the workshop furniture, or distances between objects, nor does it track the camera wearer's left hand as it pushes the wood forward over the saw in frame 2 and retracts in frame 3. Furthermore, it completely fails to detect the body or hands of the crouched coworker located ~1.5–3.0 m away on the right in frames 3–5, offering no indication from the map alone that the coworker is bent over facing the wooden structure, looking toward the camera wearer, and reaching toward the panels in front of them. Although the single hand skeleton in frame 1 clarifies the exact articulated finger and wrist configuration holding the wooden strip against the sunlit floor better than RGB alone, the pose map is severely unreliable due to extreme egocentric foreshortening, top-down viewing angles, self-occlusion of the coworker's hunched body, and motion blur across frames 2–5.
